# Independent audit: central tetrahedral sections and two-coordinate capacities

Audited source:
`candidate 3ed628996d1cbb09`.

**Result: PASS in its stated scope.** No substantive correction is needed.
This proves an ordinary tetrahedron depth formula and an exact
two-coordinate capacity statement. It does not prove a general
mixed-integer depth theorem or a three-coordinate arbitrary-law theorem.

## 1. Quadrilateral section centroid and determinant

The four displayed intersection points lie on the four captured-to-missed
edges. Their two diagonal segments meet at `(x,y,z,w)/S`, with all
coefficients strictly positive. If a quadrilateral has cyclic vertices
A,B,C,D and diagonal intersection e, its centroid is
`(A+B+C+D-e)/3`: triangulate along AC and use that the triangle area
weights are the complementary coefficients expressing e on BD. This
justifies (2), including non-parallelogram sections.

The three tetrahedra used for (3) are a valid dissection of the captured
polytope. Equivalently the captured part is a cone from vertex 0 over
the section together with the tetrahedron `(0,1,C,D)`. Their interiors
are disjoint. Direct determinant substitution gives the displayed
formula (3), with no distinct-height assumption.

An independent symbolic computation verifies all of the following as
identical rational functions, not merely numerical evaluations:

* the determinant sum equals (3);
* `(1-3 lambda_1)S(y+z)(y+w)=c`;
* the difference in (5) equals its stated positive-polynomial expression.

All cleared factors are positive. The polynomial A has positive
coefficients and positive arguments, so the asserted strictness follows
from `bA>0`, even when `lambda_1=1/3`.

## 2. Complete boundary-incidence enumeration

A proper section through an interior point has a positive and a negative
vertex value. If neither strict sign class has size one, both have size
two and no value is zero; this is exactly Section 1. Otherwise one closed
side is a vertex tetrahedron, possibly with one or two edge intercepts
equal to one. Its section remains a genuine triangle of positive area.

The complementary calculation (7) is valid for every strictly captured
vertex r, including when other vertices lie on the plane. Its three
AM--GM factors are nonnegative and sum to one. Thus (8) covers every
proper incidence without discarding a potentially minimizing direction.
The boundary plane has zero three-dimensional volume, so use of closed
caps is consistent throughout.

## 3. Orientation differentiation, including vertex cuts

Here is an explicit dominated-convergence proof of the step in Section 3.
Fix the minimizing unit normal n and write points as

    x=b+s+tn,     s in n-perpendicular.

For any tangent vector v perpendicular to n, replace the normal by
`n+h v`. Normalization of this vector is unnecessary because it defines
the same halfspace. Its inequality becomes

    t>=-h v dot s.

Consequently the signed difference in captured volume, divided by h, is
the integral over s of the signed average of the indicator of the
tetrahedron on the interval between 0 and `-h v dot s`, multiplied by
`v dot s`. All relevant s lie in one fixed compact orthogonal projection.
The absolute value of this quotient is bounded by `|v dot s|` there.

For almost every s, the point b+s is either in the relative interior of
the section or outside that section. In the first case it lies in the
interior of the tetrahedron; in the second it lies outside the compact
tetrahedron. The only excluded s form the relative boundary of the
proper two-dimensional section, a finite union of segments and hence
a set of two-dimensional measure zero. The indicator averages therefore
converge respectively to one and zero. Dominated convergence proves

    derivative = integral_section v dot(x-b) dH_2(x).

This proof is unchanged if the section passes through vertices or an
edge. No facet can coincide with this plane, since b is an interior
point. Vanishing in all tangent directions makes the section first
moment parallel to n; it also lies in n-perpendicular, so it vanishes.
Thus the section centroid is exactly b.

Continuity of cap volume on the unit sphere follows independently by
dominated convergence, because the exceptional limiting plane has
three-dimensional measure zero. Compactness gives a minimizing
direction. Shrinking an arbitrary containing cap to its through-b cap
can only decrease its volume. These facts establish attainment and
justify applying (8) to an actual minimum.

## 4. Upper construction and exact depth

The three intercepts `eta_j=3b_j` are positive and at most one. They
are not collinear and determine a proper vertex-cap plane. Their average
has coordinates b, including the remaining coordinate at the selected
largest-coordinate vertex. Hence this plane passes through b and its
cap realizes the stated product. Intercepts equal to one introduce only
closed-boundary vertices and do not change the determinant. Together
with the lower bound, this proves the exact depth formula (9).

## 5. Exact two-coordinate face

For a downward-dominated row vector, raising to `p=d/(d-1)` and dropping
the at-most-one entry in the other selected column gives precisely the
two `(d-1)`-variable geometric means in the source. Superadditivity of
the geometric mean then bounds their sum by one. This remains valid
when some factors vanish and when d=2, where that geometric mean is
one-dimensional and the assertion is simply an equality.

The proposed construction has zero diagonal, nonnegative entries, and
column sums exactly one. Its first two row geometric means are
`theta^((d-1)/d)` and `(1-theta)^((d-1)/d)`; all other row means vanish.
It therefore supplies sufficiency throughout the closed face, including
its endpoints. For d=1 the unique off-diagonal stochastic matrix has
row means `(1,1)`, so its downward set is exactly the stated square.

## 6. Probability capacities

The capacity definition implies each pointwise probability upper bound
without requiring that the infimum be attained. The two closed events
cover the probability space because `U>t` and `V>1-t` cannot both hold.
Overlaps are harmless for the union bound. When both capacities are
positive, differentiation of the strictly convex two-term polynomial
places its minimum at the stated interior t, with value
`(a^p+b^p)^(1-d)`. Zero capacities and d=1 were separately handled.

For a column-stochastic matrix with at most two nonzero rows, evaluating
those rows on any barycentric point makes their values sum to one.
The remaining rows are identically zero and their capacities equal
zero. Thus the final matrix corollary follows exactly. No unproved
promotion from two rows to three is used.
